dossier.audience_name: Customer Success / Ops teams revamping intake forms at fast-growing SaaS companies
dossier.orientation: Tally is a no-code form builder a Customer Success or Ops person can use to build a structured customer request/feedback form and pass submissions into the tools their team already works in.

setup_conditions: Build the intake form in the Tally editor (block-based, typing "/" to insert fields), optionally generating or editing it in plain language with Tally AI (E7)
Configure conditional logic so the form branches by request type and collects the fields the actioning team needs (E8)
Connect the form to the downstream destination through the published Zapier integration, or via Tally's API where a team prefers programmatic handling (E9, E10)
Stay within the documented fair usage guidelines to keep unlimited forms and submissions free (E3, E13)
decision_gaps: Which of the named destinations (ticketing, Notion, Airtable, Slack, CRM) have a documented native Tally integration rather than only a Zapier path?
Are the Zapier integration and the API available on the free plan, or do they require Pro or Business?
defining_need_fit.supported_core_workflow: Capture structured customer requests and feedback and route them into an existing CS process without engineering involvement
defining_need_fit.caveat: Routing is documented through Zapier's 2,000+ app catalogue and an API; the depth or nativeness of any one destination connector, and field-level mapping into a specific ticketing system, is not established by the selected evidence.
defining_need_fit.why: Documented block-based no-code building, conditional logic for structured capture, and a Zapier/API hand-off cover the whole stated task of capturing structured requests and moving them into an existing CS workflow without engineering.

ranked_relevance.why: Conditional logic is the documented mechanism that makes one intake form collect request-type-specific information instead of a universal field set.
The Zapier integration is the documented no-code route from a submission into the team's existing downstream tools.
A named customer used Tally forms to collect product feedback with 30%+ response rates, the closest documented outcome to structured feedback capture.
The API states how forms and submissions can be handled programmatically when a team wants more than the Zapier path.
Plain-language generation and editing describes how a non-engineer builds or revises the intake form.
Unlimited forms and submissions free within fair usage guidelines supports standing up several request-type forms at ordinary volume.
Same offer stated in the features documentation, with the fair-usage condition attached.
EU-based GDPR compliance and European data storage answers the data-handling question a CS team faces when customer submissions are captured.
Automatic submission deletion after a set period is the documented retention control for teams with privacy-framework requirements, on Business.
Named company adoption, including the automation company in the audience research, is non-quantified but relevant social proof.
30-day version history is relevant to teams revising intake forms, but no researched problem concerns reverting form changes.
Duplicate statement of the Pro 30-day version history with the free-plan 7-day comparison.
90-day version history on Business is plan-tier detail, not tied to the intake task.
Email verification is framed as lead capture and conversion, which is adjacent to a CS intake decision.
Pro price in euros is needed for a budget conversation but is not itself relevant to the workflow.
Business price in euros is background for the retention-control tier.
Pro price in dollars; currency and billing basis differ from E14, so treat as pricing background only.
Business price in dollars with Pro features included; pricing background.
True and licensed, but a 10MB free-plan upload cap is a limitation detail no researched problem raises.
Removing the upload size limit matters only if attachments are central, which this audience's research does not establish.
Stripe checkout forms are a payments capability unrelated to CS request intake.
A digital creator's general praise is not a description of what the product does and carries no CS-team relevance for a solution-aware evaluator.

problem_fits.caveat: Conditional branching is documented as a mechanism; whether it produces the exact field set each actioning owner wants is a design question, and the source is a single 2022-12-20 discussion whose present applicability is uncorroborated.
problem_fits.why: Dynamic forms that adapt based on inputs are the documented way one form asks the request-type-specific questions a universal form misses.

problem_fits.caveat: Conditional logic can require the same information from an internal submitter as from a customer, but the selected evidence proves no reduction in time-to-resolution or in staff-submitted tickets, and this single undated source describes another vendor's form.
problem_fits.why: The information-parity gap is a form-design problem that documented branching logic can address, without any licensed outcome claim.

segment_objections.objection: Our requests have to land in our existing ticketing system, Notion, Airtable, Slack or CRM — does Tally actually connect to ours without an engineer?
segment_objections.answer: Tally documents a Zapier integration reaching 2,000+ web apps and an API for programmatically creating, updating or deleting forms and submissions; native connector coverage for any specific one of those tools is not established by the selected evidence.
